about.metaDescription: Usha is the company behind Usha Platform — the platform for human expression. Get to know the vision and where we're headed.
about.title: About us
about.lead: Usha is the company behind Usha Platform — the platform for human expression.
about.p1: We believe the best moments happen when people meet for real — in movement, in play, and in creating together. Usha Platform brings creators, venues and participants together in one place, where passion meets professionalism and every booking feels safe. Creators are identity-verified and all payments are handled securely, so you can focus on what actually matters: the experience.
about.p2: Usha was founded by Pablo Acosta, who works at the intersection of dance, technology and community-building. The vision is simple: to build a place where creativity can thrive, talent can be seen, and people can come closer together.
about.p3: We're building step by step, with real experiences from day one. The foundation is recurring nights in Stockholm — open dance training every week, where everyone is welcome regardless of level. From there we grow into monthly parties and, further ahead, an annual festival that brings the whole community together.
about.closing: This is just the beginning. Welcome to join us from the start.

faq.title: Questions &
faq.a1: On sold tickets we take 3.5% + SEK 3.50 per ticket in commission, the same for everyone. Free events cost nothing. You always see your share before you publish.
faq.a2: Hosts and creators verify with BankID — it keeps everyone safe. Attendees can usually buy a ticket without verifying.
faq.a3: Ticket money goes through Stripe. It is transferred the day after the night and is usually in the account within a couple of days.
faq.q4: Can guests buy without an account?
faq.a4: Yes. Guests can buy a ticket with just an email and get a QR code to show at the door — no account needed.
faq.q5: Can I get help from others?
faq.a5: Yes, in two ways. Per event you invite your crew (creators, taxi dancers, volunteers, co-hosts), delegate ticket scanning and agree on fees. If you run a venue you can also build a team for the venue itself and decide what each person may do — the finances always stay with you.

steps.title: How it works
steps.s1Body: Sign up as a venue and fill in your venue page: name, image, address and a few lines about you. It takes a few minutes and costs nothing.
steps.s2Body: We talk through how you want it to work and sign a separate agreement with you. It sets out what applies to your venue.
steps.s3Title: Organisers put on nights at your venue
steps.s3Body: When an organiser names you as the venue, you get a request. You approve it or decline. If you want to put on your own nights, you do that yourselves; the account then needs to be verified with BankID.
steps.s4Body: Guests get their ticket with a QR code by email. At the door you check them in with an ordinary phone, and your staff can be allowed to scan.
steps.s5Body: Each night is settled on its own, with a statement. The money is transferred the day after the night and is usually in the account within a couple of days.

control.title: You decide over your venue

control.approvalBody: Nothing appears on your page until you have approved it under Requests. An approval covers one event at a time.
control.teamBody: Invite colleagues and choose what each of them can do: create events, see bookings, scan at the door, send messages, see statistics or manage the venue page. The finances always stay with the owner account.
control.pageBody: Your own page on usha.se gathers the nights at your venue, upcoming ones first. You can share it in your own channels.
control.followersBody: Visitors can follow you. When a new night at your venue is approved, your followers get an email about it.

cost.title: What it costs
cost.freeSub: for the profile, no monthly fee
cost.fee: Whoever sells tickets pays 3.5% + SEK 3.50 per ticket sold.
cost.agreementBody: We agree the terms in a separate agreement with each venue. There is no standard model. One venue shares the revenue, another rents out the space and a third lends it for free as marketing.
cost.payout: If you get a share of the night, the money is transferred the day after the night and is usually in the account within a couple of days.
cost.payee: To receive money, the venue needs to be a limited company, a sole trader or an association with a Swedish organisation number and F-tax.

faq.title: Questions &
faq.q1: What does it cost to be a venue?
faq.a1: The profile is free and there is no monthly fee. Whoever sells tickets pays 3.5% + SEK 3.50 per ticket. Everything else is in your agreement.
faq.q2: Can anything appear at our venue without our yes?
faq.a2: No. A night an organiser puts on at your venue lands under Requests and only appears on your page once you have approved it.
faq.a3: Not to approve other people's nights. To put on your own nights, the account needs to be verified with BankID.
faq.q4: When do we get the money?
faq.a4: Each night is settled on its own. The money is transferred the day after the night and is usually in the account within a couple of days.
faq.a5: A limited company, a sole trader or an association with a Swedish organisation number and F-tax. We check this before the first payout.
faq.q6: Can staff help without seeing the finances?
faq.a6: Yes. In the venue team you choose what each person can do, for example scan at the door or put on nights. Payouts and company details cannot be shared.

securityPage.title: Security
securityPage.metaDescription: How Usha Platform protects accounts, payments and personal data: BankID, data in the EU, encryption, backups, independent monthly checks.
securityPage.intro: Usha Platform is run by Usha AB in Stockholm. This page says what we do to protect your data – briefly and verifiably. Everything here is also written down in our security programme, and we measure it automatically every month.
securityPage.identityBody: You sign in with Mobile BankID, Google or email. Anything that requires us to know who you are – selling tickets, scanning at the door, signing agreements, volunteering – requires a BankID-verified account. Personal identity numbers are stored hashed only and never read by the app in clear text.
securityPage.dataBody: Database, login and files are hosted by Supabase in Frankfurt (EU). All traffic is encrypted (TLS, HSTS), data is encrypted at rest. Every table has row-level security: a user can only reach their own rows, and this is checked automatically every month.
securityPage.paymentsBody: Payments are handled by Stripe. Card details never pass through our servers – we only see that a payment went through. Sellers are paid via Stripe Connect after Stripe's own identity checks.
securityPage.backupBody: The database is backed up daily by Supabase. Uploaded files are copied every night to Cloudflare in the EU with a 30-day archive, and we are alerted if the copy fails.
securityPage.monitoringBody: Errors are reported to Sentry (EU). On the first of every month an automatic check runs over our safeguards – code protection, vulnerabilities, access, backups, database rules, email protection (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) – and the result is archived with a timestamp. Access to systems is reviewed every quarter.
securityPage.developmentBody: No change goes straight to production: all code is reviewed through pull requests, tested automatically and built before release. The main branch is protected and dependencies are monitored for known vulnerabilities.
securityPage.vendorsIntro: These companies process data on our behalf. All have data processing agreements and independent attestations you can read on their own trust pages.
securityPage.complianceBody: We follow the GDPR and Swedish law. We do not hold a SOC 2 or ISO 27001 attestation today – that suits a different size of company – but we work by the same principle: controls are written down, measured automatically and evidence is kept. If you need an extract for a procurement, get in touch.
securityPage.rightsBody: You can view, correct, export and delete your data. Account deletion is done in the app under My account and removes what can be removed immediately. How we process personal data is described in the
securityPage.reportBody: If you have discovered a vulnerability or something that looks wrong, we want to know. Write to us – we reply within two working days and tell you what we did.

The seller's cancellation rules: The seller sets the cancellation rules for each event and service. The rules and the cancellation deadline are shown on the offer and at checkout before you buy. If no deadline has been set, you can cancel until the start.

No right of withdrawal for fixed dates: Tickets and bookings for an event, a course, an experience or another leisure activity that takes place on a specific date or within a specific period have no right of withdrawal, under Chapter 2, Section 11(12) of the Swedish Distance Contracts Act (2005:59). You can still cancel according to the seller's rules.

Right of withdrawal for punch cards and memberships: If you buy a punch card, a membership or anything else without a fixed date from a seller that is a business (trader), you have a 14-day right of withdrawal from the date of purchase. You withdraw from the purchase with the Withdraw from the purchase button on the booking in the Platform, with the Swedish Consumer Agency's (Konsumentverket) standard withdrawal form or by emailing support@usha.se. You will receive a confirmation by email. If you withdraw from the purchase, you get back what you paid, including the service fee, no later than 14 days after we have received your notice. If you asked at checkout to start using the card straight away and then used classes before withdrawing, a proportionate part of the price is deducted for the classes you used. If you did not make that request, nothing is deducted.

Punch card validity: A punch card is valid for as many months as it has classes, counted from the date of purchase. The last day of validity is shown at checkout, on the receipt and on the card. Classes that you do not use before the last day of validity expire and are not refunded. If the seller cancels one or more sessions during the card's validity period, the last day of validity is extended by one week for each cancelled session. A break that was not stated in the offer when you bought the card counts as cancelled sessions. If the seller discontinues the series so that there are no sessions left on which to use the classes, you get back the money for the remaining classes. Cards sold without a last day of validity remain valid as before.

If the seller cancels: If an event is cancelled, you get back the full amount, including the service fee. If the event is moved to another date, you can choose between keeping the ticket and getting back the full amount.

Refunds: The money is refunded to the same payment method you used. Card payments normally appear on your account within 5–10 banking days. More about how this works is available at usha.se/refund-policy.

If you cannot agree: Contact the seller first. If you get no reply, or if you cannot agree, email support@usha.se with your booking ID. Usha will then help sort out the matter and can carry out the refund via the Platform. Your statutory rights are not affected.

privacy.s1Body: Usha AB is the data controller for the processing of your personal data. We process your data in accordance with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and Swedish law.
privacy.s2Items:
Account details: name, email address, profile picture

Booking history: dates, times, services you have booked
Communication: messages via the platform

privacy.s3Items:

Manage bookings and payments
Send confirmations and notifications
Prevent fraud and abuse
Comply with legal obligations
privacy.s4Body: We process your data based on: performance of a contract (to deliver the service), legitimate interest (to improve the platform), consent (for marketing) and legal obligation (accounting).
privacy.s5Body: We share your data with: Stripe (payment processing), Supabase (data storage), Vercel (website hosting), Cloudflare (scheduled jobs and backups of uploaded files), Resend (email delivery), Signicat (BankID login and identification), Sentry (error reports: when you send a report yourself with the “Something not working?” button, Sentry receives your description, the page address and technical information about your device, and a picture of the page if you tick that box. All text, images and QR codes are hidden in the picture. The data is stored in the EU; Sentry is a US company and any transfer to the US takes place under the EU–US Data Privacy Framework and the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses. We process the reports on the basis of our legitimate interest in finding and fixing errors), Google (visitor statistics via Google Analytics, with cookies only if you have accepted them, and encrypted storage of backups; Google cannot read the contents). We never sell your personal data to third parties. Data may be shared with authorities if required by law.
privacy.s6Body: We keep your data for as long as your account is active. When you delete your account, your personal data is anonymised and hidden immediately: your profile is removed from all public areas, your login is blocked and the link to your email address and BankID is released so you can register again. Data we are legally required to keep (e.g. payment and accounting records for 7 years) is retained for the statutory period and then erased. This action cannot be undone. Backups of the database are stored encrypted for no more than 14 days and are then overwritten. Data you have deleted may therefore remain in a backup for up to 14 days, but it is not used and is not brought back if a backup is restored. Error reports and pictures sent with the “Something not working?” button are deleted automatically after 30 days.

Restrict the processing of your data
Object to processing
Request data portability
Withdraw consent

refundPolicy.heading: Refund Policy
refundPolicy.overviewBody: Usha mediates bookings between buyers and sellers (creators, organisers and venues) and sells its own events. Here we explain how cancellation, the right of withdrawal and refunds work. The rules that apply are set out in the terms of use, section 5. Tickets for events on a specific date have no right of withdrawal, but you can cancel according to the seller's rules. Punch cards and memberships have a 14-day right of withdrawal. Money is always refunded to the same payment method you used.
refundPolicy.cancellationPendingBody: You can cancel yourself until the cancellation deadline the seller has set. The deadline is shown on the offer before you buy. If no deadline has been set, you can cancel until the start. The seller can always cancel. You then get back the full amount, including the service fee.
refundPolicy.cancellationConfirmedBody: After the cancellation deadline you cannot cancel yourself. Contact the seller. If the seller cancels, you get back the full amount. You can withdraw from punch cards and memberships yourself within 14 days of purchase, see below.
refundPolicy.cancellationCompletedBody1: A booking that has already taken place cannot be cancelled via the Platform. Contact the seller or email
refundPolicy.cancellationCompletedBody2: and we will help sort out the matter.
refundPolicy.danceBody1: A punch card is valid for as many months as it has classes, counted from the date of purchase, and the last day of validity is shown on the card and on the receipt.
refundPolicy.danceBodyStrong: Classes that are not used before the last day of validity expire and are not refunded
refundPolicy.danceBody2: If the seller cancels one or more sessions during the validity period, the card is extended by one week for each cancelled session. A break that was not stated in the offer when you bought counts as cancelled sessions. If the seller discontinues the series, you get back the money for the remaining classes. Within 14 days of purchase you can withdraw from the card with the Withdraw from the purchase button on the booking or by emailing support@usha.se. You then get back what you paid, including the service fee. If you asked at checkout to start using the card straight away, a proportionate part is deducted for the classes you have already used. Otherwise nothing is deducted.
refundPolicy.b2bBody: A request that has not yet been approved can be withdrawn at no cost. Once the request has been approved and paid, the same rules as above apply: the full amount back if the booking is cancelled before it has taken place. The right of withdrawal does not apply between businesses.
refundPolicy.timelineBody1: The refund starts when the booking is cancelled or withdrawn from, and no later than within 14 days. Card payments normally appear on your account within
refundPolicy.timelineBody2: depending on your bank and card issuer. Swish payments are refunded to the same Swish number.
refundPolicy.disputesBody1: If you and the seller cannot agree, or if a refund has not arrived after 10 banking days, email
refundPolicy.disputesBody2: with the booking ID and a brief description. We will help sort out the matter. If we cannot agree, you as a consumer can turn to the Swedish National Board for Consumer Disputes (Allmänna reklamationsnämnden, ARN), Box 174, 101 23 Stockholm, Sweden, arn.se. ARN handles disputes between consumers and businesses free of charge.
refundPolicy.platformFeeBody: If an event is cancelled, the seller cancels, or you withdraw from a punch card or membership within the withdrawal period, you get back the full amount, including the service fee. Usha's commission from the seller is then also returned, so no party bears the cost of a proper cancellation. Cases where fraud or abuse is suspected are investigated separately.

hero.body: As a taxi dancer you dance with the guests at our evenings – especially those who are new or standing on the side. You volunteer and choose your own shifts.
hero.note: Taxi dancers verify with Mobile BankID. Age limit 18.

value.heading: Why be a taxi dancer with us?
value.paidTitle: Free entry and a meal voucher
value.paidBody: You volunteer and are not paid. You get free entry and one meal voucher per evening: food and a non-alcoholic drink at the after-work.
value.bankidBody: All taxi dancers confirm identity and age with Mobile BankID. It builds trust between guests, organiser and dancers.
value.packagesBody: Shifts are between 17:00 and 23:00 and at least two hours. Sign up, check in when you arrive and cancel by 10:00 on the day if something comes up.

how.heading: How it works
how.customersStep1: Come to the evening as usual.
how.customersStep2: The taxi dancers are on the dance floor – ask for a dance, whatever your level.
how.customersStep3: Taxi dancing is part of the evening.
how.customersStep4: All taxi dancers are BankID verified and 18 or older.
how.organizersTitle: How to become a taxi dancer
how.organizersStep1: Create an account on Usha and verify with Mobile BankID.
how.organizersStep2: Pick the shifts you can do between 17:00 and 23:00.
how.organizersStep3: Check in in the app when you arrive.
how.organizersStep4: Cancel by 10:00 on the day if something comes up.

positioning.heading: What taxi dancing is — and is not
positioning.body: A taxi dancer is a dance partner for partner dancing – kizomba, swing, salsa, tango and more – at our dance evenings. It does not include sexual or intimate contact. Use beyond this breaks Usha Platform’s terms of use and leads to suspension.

meta.description: A guide for creators and venues: create an account, verify yourself, publish and get paid.

guide.title: Getting started with Usha Platform
guide.intro: This guide takes you from an empty account to your first booking. Read the parts that apply to you — creator, venue, or both.

s1.title: Create an account
s1.p1: Go to usha.se and choose Get started. You can sign up with Google, Facebook or an email address — it takes seconds.
s1.roleTitle: Pick the right role straight away
s1.roleBody: You choose a role when you sign up, and that choice drives the whole app: what you see, what you can create and how you get paid.
s1.creator: Creator — you offer services: dance, photography, music, workshops.
s1.venue: Venue — you run a place and want to fill it with events.
s1.customer: Audience — you want to book things and go to them.
s1.roleNote: If you pick the wrong one you can change it later under Settings → Account. But it is easier to get it right from the start, and this is the most common mistake we see.
s1.companyBody: If you sell anything you also say whether you do it as an individual or through a company. Companies verify their registration number and appear with it on the receipt. You can change this later.

s2.title: Verify yourself
s2.p1: Everyone who puts something up for sale on the platform verifies their identity with Swedish Mobile BankID. It is not a formality — it is the whole reason a stranger dares to book you.
s2.p2: You will find it under Profile. It takes under a minute and only has to be done once.
s2.companyBody: Also enter your registration number under Profile and press Verify company. We check it against the EU business register and fill in the legal name automatically.

creators.title: If you are a creator
creators.profileBody: A picture, a short text about what you do, and where you are based. Your profile is what people see before they book, so a few minutes here are well spent.
creators.servicesBody: A service is something someone can book: a private lesson, a photo session, a DJ set. Set a price and a length.
creators.calendarBody: Mark when you are available and people can book those times directly without asking first. You can subscribe to your Usha calendar from your phone.
creators.eventsBody: Running a course or an evening? Create an event with tickets instead. Every ticket gets a QR code you scan at the door.

venues.title: If you run a venue
venues.pageBody: You get your own page where your events are gathered. Visitors can follow you and then hear when something new is coming up at your place.
venues.eventsBody: Create events, set ticket prices and sell directly. You can have several ticket types on the same evening — for example workshop, social dancing, or both.
venues.requestsBody: When someone else posts an event and names you as the venue it lands under Requests. Nothing shows on your page until you approve it. An approval covers that event — the organiser keeps their event, you get the visibility.
venues.teamBody: Under The team you invite people and decide what each of them may do: create events, see bookings, scan at the door, send messages, see statistics or manage the venue page. There are ready-made presets if you would rather not tick boxes.
venues.teamNote: The finances can never be handed out. Payouts, Stripe and company details belong to the owner account and cannot be ticked for anyone else. If someone else is to handle the finances that is a change of owner, not a permission.

money.title: The money
money.stripeBody: Go to Payouts and press Connect Stripe account. Stripe asks for your details and bank account and verifies you. That is their requirement under money-laundering rules, and the one step nobody can do for you.
money.commissionBody: We take 3.5 percent plus SEK 3.50 per sold ticket in commission, the same for everyone. Free events cost nothing. You always see your share before you publish.
money.betaNote: During the beta all plans are free.
money.payoutBody: The money goes through Stripe to your account. It is transferred the day after the night and is usually in the account within a couple of days.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.a1: Yes, if you sell something. People who only buy a ticket do not.
faq.q2: Can guests buy without an account?
faq.a2: Yes. They give an email address and get a QR code to show at the door.
faq.q3: I picked the wrong role when signing up
faq.a3: Go to Settings → Account and change it under Your role.
faq.q4: Can several people manage the same account?
faq.a4: Venues can build a team and hand out permissions. Creators can invite co-organisers and crew per event.
faq.q5: What if I have to cancel?
faq.a5: You can refund the tickets from the event. Attendees are told automatically.

compare.metaTitle: Usha compared with Tickster and Billetto – fees and features
compare.metaDescription: Fees, payment methods, check-in, punch cards and BankID side by side, taken from the companies' own pages with a date. And when Usha is not the right fit.
compare.ogTitle: Usha compared with Tickster and Billetto
compare.heroTitle: Usha compared with Tickster and Billetto
compare.heroBody: Choosing a ticketing service should not mean doing the research yourself. Here we stand next to two of the most common ones in Sweden, row by row. Everything about them comes from their own public pages, and we say just as clearly when Usha is not the right choice.
compare.tableNote: The details about Tickster and Billetto were copied from their public pages on {date}. If you find something that is wrong, write to us and we will correct it.

buyerFee.label: Fee paid by the buyer
buyerFee.usha: None by default. The organiser can choose a service fee of 2% + SEK 2.50 per order, the same whatever the payment method.
buyerFee.tickster: Set per organiser: per ticket, per order or none at all. No public rate. In a current example, SEK 30 on a SEK 259 ticket.
buyerFee.billetto: 3.99% + SEK 7.99 per ticket excluding VAT, no cap stated. The organiser can choose to absorb the fee.

organiserFee.label: Fee paid by the organiser
organiserFee.usha: 3.5% + SEK 3.50 per sold ticket. The same for everyone, no tier to buy.
organiserFee.tickster: A variable cost per sold ticket, priced by quote. No fixed costs, except hardware rental.
organiserFee.billetto: None beyond the buyer's fee. Swish costs the organiser SEK 5 per order excluding VAT.

freeEvents.label: Free events
freeEvents.tickster: If you sell nothing it costs nothing, according to their site. We found no separate rule for free events.
freeEvents.billetto: Can be listed, but the buyer pays a platform fee whose amount is not stated.

monthly.label: Fixed cost
monthly.tickster: No fixed costs, according to their pricing page.
monthly.billetto: No monthly fee, no setup cost.

payment.label: Payment methods for the buyer
payment.usha: Card, Apple Pay and Google Pay. Klarna from SEK 1,000. Swish at events Usha runs itself.
payment.tickster: Card, Swish, credit invoice, instalments and advance invoice.
payment.billetto: Card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Swish, Klarna, PayPal and e-invoice, when the organiser has enabled them.

payout.label: Payout
payout.usha: The money goes through Stripe. It is transferred the day after the night and is usually in the account within a couple of days.
payout.billetto: 3–5 business days after the event. Card purchases continuously via Stripe Connect; Swish and PayPal after the event.

door.label: Check-in at the door
door.usha: Included. QR ticket by email, scanning with any phone, and you can let others scan.
door.tickster: Their own organiser app scans QR codes with a phone, plus scanning hardware for larger entrances.
door.billetto: App for iOS and Android that scans QR codes and shows the guest list, with door sales.

kiosk.label: Self check-in
kiosk.usha: Yes. A tablet at the door where the guest scans themselves, no staff needed. Included.

passes.label: Punch cards and season passes
passes.usha: Punch cards with a validity period and one punch per night, also across a whole series.
passes.tickster: Season and annual passes, ticket pools and points. Punch cards are not mentioned.
passes.billetto: Monthly or annual memberships and season passes. Ticket bundles give separate tickets. Punch cards are not mentioned.

venueShare.label: Sharing with the venue
venueShare.usha: Calculated per night, with records you can export.

bankid.label: BankID
bankid.usha: Log in and create an account with Mobile BankID, no password. Age check where required.
bankid.tickster: Account created by email. BankID only as the bank's check at payment. ID is shown at the door.
bankid.billetto: Email, Facebook or Google for the organiser. Buyers can purchase without an account. No BankID.

marketing.label: Reaching the audience
marketing.usha: A page for every event and creator, a public calendar and followers by email. No SMS.
marketing.tickster: Email and SMS to buyers, audiences and event search across Sweden.
marketing.billetto: Email and SMS, a marketplace and followers who become contacts. Advertising is on by default and costs 33% on the tickets it drives.

fitFor.label: Best suited for
fitFor.usha: Recurring nights, classes and small venues where the same guests come back.
fitFor.tickster: Festivals, culture, arenas and larger venues. Contact with sales to get started.
fitFor.billetto: Self-service for everyone, including private individuals. Two tiers, under and over 1,000 tickets per year.

compare.fit1: Recurring nights, classes and series where the same guests come back and a punch card makes a difference.
compare.fit2: Small and mid-sized venues that want the split with the organiser calculated per night.
compare.fit3: Anyone who wants guests to check themselves in at the door, without staff.
compare.fit4: Creators who want to start tonight, without a sales meeting or a monthly fee.
compare.notFit1: Festivals and arenas with tens of thousands of tickets and hardware at the entrance.
compare.notFit2: If you need Swish at your own events right now. Today Swish is only available at nights Usha runs itself.
compare.notFit3: If you want to reach buyers by SMS, or need invoicing and instalments at checkout.
compare.notFit4: If your audience already finds you on Tickster's or Billetto's marketplace and that is where they buy.
compare.notFitFootnote: We would rather say this now than have you find out after the first night.
compare.faq1Q: What does it cost to sell tickets on Usha?
compare.faq1A: 3.5% + SEK 3.50 per sold ticket, the same for everyone. On a SEK 130 ticket that is SEK 8.05. Free events cost nothing and there is no monthly fee or tier to buy.
compare.faq2Q: Does Usha charge the buyer a fee?
compare.faq2A: Not by default. The organiser can choose to let the buyer pay a service fee of 2% + SEK 2.50 per order; it is then shown clearly at checkout before the purchase, and the fee is the same whatever the payment method.
compare.faq3Q: Why do you compare yourselves with Tickster and Billetto?
compare.faq3A: Because they are the ones most people ask about. We copy from their public pages and state the date, so you can check for yourself. If you find an error we will correct it.
compare.faq4Q: Can I move my events from Tickster or Billetto to Usha?
compare.faq4A: Yes. List the event with us and share the link, and guests buy here. Tickets already sold with the old provider remain valid there; upcoming nights you sell here.
compare.sourcesBody: Read on {date}. Tickster publishes no amounts; its fee is set per organiser. Billetto publishes its price list.
